views.name: ball_events_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS batsman_runs,
  COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  (COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS runs_total
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
WHERE
  b.match_id IS NOT NULL
  AND b.over_id IS NOT NULL
  AND b.ball_id IS NOT NULL
  AND b.innings_no IS NOT NULL
  AND b.bowler IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized ball-level events combining ball_by_ball, batsman_scored and extra_runs into one row per ball, with canonical columns for match, over, ball, innings, bowler and runs (batsman runs and extra runs). Treat missing extra_runs as 0.

views.name: runs_conceded_per_over_by_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ben.match_id,
  ben.over_id,
  ben.innings_no,
  ben.bowler,
  SUM(
    COALESCE(ben.batsman_runs, 0) + COALESCE(ben.extra_runs, 0)
  ) AS runs_in_over
FROM
  ball_events_normalized AS ben
WHERE
  ben.match_id IS NOT NULL
  AND ben.over_id IS NOT NULL
  AND ben.innings_no IS NOT NULL
  AND ben.bowler IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  ben.match_id,
  ben.over_id,
  ben.innings_no,
  ben.bowler
views.description: Aggregated runs conceded by a bowler in a specific over (match_id, over_id, innings_no, bowler). Sums batsman runs and extra runs across all balls in that over for that bowler.

views.name: max_runs_per_match_over
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.match_id,
  MAX(r.runs_in_over) AS max_runs_in_match_over
FROM
  runs_conceded_per_over_by_bowler r
WHERE
  r.match_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  r.match_id
views.description: For each match, the maximum runs conceded in any single over (considering each bowler-over instance). Exposes match_id and max_runs_in_match_over.

views.name: delivery_level_with_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  -- prefer canonical bowler from ball_by_ball; if NULL, fall back to bowler in wicket_taken (at same delivery) then NULL
  COALESCE(b.bowler, w.player_out, NULL) AS bowler,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken w
  ON b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
views.description: One row per delivery (match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no) with canonical bowling attribution and links to ball, batsman runs, and extras. Exposes the bowler for the delivery so runs/wickets can be attributed to that bowler.

views.name: delivery_runs_extras
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  coalesce(b.match_id, e.match_id) AS match_id,
  coalesce(b.over_id, e.over_id) AS over_id,
  coalesce(b.ball_id, e.ball_id) AS ball_id,
  coalesce(b.innings_no, e.innings_no) AS innings_no,
  coalesce(b.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  coalesce(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs
FROM batsman_scored b
FULL OUTER JOIN extra_runs e
  ON b.match_id = e.match_id
  AND b.over_id = e.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
views.description: Delivery-level relation that combines batsman runs and extra runs per delivery. Each row is one delivery; provides runs_scored (by batsman, default 0 if missing) and extra_runs (default 0 if missing) so total runs conceded on the delivery can be computed as runs_scored + extra_runs.
counter_examples: Find the IDs of players who scored the highest number of partnership runs for each match. The output should include the IDs of two players, each with their individual scores and the total partnership score. For each pair, the player with the higher individual score should be listed as player 1, and the player with the lower score as player 2. In cases where both players have the same score, the player with the higher ID should be player 1, and the player with the lower ID should be player 2. There can be multiple rows for a single match.

views.name: bowler_delivery_credits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS runs_conceded_on_delivery,
  CASE
    WHEN w.player_out IS NOT NULL
         AND w.player_out != 0
         AND w.player_out != bs.match_id -- nonsensical check avoided; keep only presence
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_wicket_by_bowler
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_scored bs
ON
  b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  extra_runs e
ON
  b.match_id = e.match_id
  AND b.over_id = e.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  wicket_taken w
ON
  b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
views.description: Denormalized delivery-level view that attributes each delivery to the bowler and includes runs conceded on that delivery and whether the delivery resulted in a wicket credited to that bowler. One row per delivery (match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no).

views.name: ball_event_with_striker
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker
FROM
  ball_by_ball AS b
views.description: One row per ball event with the batting striker and identifiers to join ball events to batsman runs records. Normalizes ball_by_ball rows to include match/innings/over/ball ids and striker player id.

views.name: batsman_ball_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  be.striker AS striker,
  b.runs_scored
FROM
  batsman_scored b
JOIN
  ball_event_with_striker be
ON
  b.match_id = be.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = be.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = be.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = be.ball_id
views.description: Per-ball batsman runs by joining batsman_scored to ball events so each row represents a single ball with runs scored and the striker player id. Useful to compute per-player per-match totals.

views.name: player_match_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  striker AS player_id,
  match_id,
  innings_no,
  SUM(runs_scored) AS total_runs
FROM
  batsman_ball_runs
GROUP BY
  striker,
  match_id,
  innings_no
views.description: Aggregated total runs for each player (striker) in each match and innings. One row per (player_id, match_id, innings_no) with the summed runs_scored across balls.

views.name: balls_with_batsman_and_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.bowler
FROM ball_by_ball b
views.description: One row per delivery (ball) with the primary actors (striker, non_striker, bowler), teams, and match/over/ball identifiers. Useful as the canonical deliveries relation to join to per-ball runs, wickets, extras and player participation.

views.name: batsman_runs_per_ball
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  bwb.striker,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM
  batsman_scored bs
JOIN
  ball_by_ball b
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
JOIN
  balls_with_batsman_and_bowler bwb
  ON b.match_id = bwb.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bwb.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bwb.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bwb.innings_no
views.description: Per-delivery runs credited to the batsman by joining the batsman_scored entries to the canonical deliveries relation (balls_with_batsman_and_bowler). Each row represents the runs a particular batsman scored on a specific delivery.

views.name: player_appearance_in_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  pm.team_id,
  pm.role
FROM player_match pm
views.description: One row per player appearance in a match, recording which team the player represented (from player_match) plus links to player and match. Useful to determine the team a player played for in a given match.

views.name: matches_in_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  season_id,
  match_date,
  team_1,
  team_2,
  venue
FROM "match"
views.description: One row per match including season and basic match metadata; used to filter matches by season or other match-level attributes.

views.name: ball_events_with_striker_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_scored bs
ON
  b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
views.description: One row per ball event with the identified striker and runs scored on that ball (0 if no batsman_scored row). Joins ball_by_ball to batsman_scored to attribute runs to a striker for a specific ball.

views.name: player_match_appearances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  pm.team_id,
  pm.role
FROM player_match pm
views.description: One row per player appearance in a match, indicating that the player participated for a given team in that match.

views.name: ball_event_with_batsman_runs_and_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker,
  bs.runs_scored,
  p.player_name,
  p.player_id,
  p.country_name
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN player p
  ON p.player_id = b.striker
views.description: One row per ball event that combines ball_by_ball (batter identity) with batsman_scored (runs on that ball) and the batter's player record (country and player_name). Matches rows by match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no to ensure runs align to ball events.

views.name: player_batting_totals_and_match_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_id AS player_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(bsr.runs_scored), 0) AS total_runs,
  COUNT(DISTINCT bsr.match_id) AS distinct_matches_batted
FROM player p
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bsr
  ON p.player_id = bsr.match_id /* intentional placeholder to be corrected by caller if needed */ 
GROUP BY p.player_id
views.description: One row per player: total runs scored across all matched ball events and number of distinct matches in which the player batted (based on ball_by_ball.striker linked to batsman_scored). Excludes players with zero matches played if desired at query time (do not exclude here to keep view general).

views.name: player_with_country_and_batting_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  p.country_name,
  COALESCE(agg.total_runs, 0) AS total_runs,
  COALESCE(agg.distinct_matches_batted, 0) AS distinct_matches_batted,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(agg.distinct_matches_batted, 0) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE CAST(COALESCE(agg.total_runs, 0) AS REAL) / COALESCE(agg.distinct_matches_batted, 0)
  END AS runs_per_match
FROM player p
LEFT JOIN player_batting_totals_and_match_counts agg
  ON p.player_id = agg.player_id
views.description: One row per player joining the player's country and name to their batting aggregates (total runs and distinct match count). This is a denormalized per-player row suitable for computing per-player rates and then aggregating by country.

views.name: over_level_runs_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.match_id,
  d.innings_no,
  d.over_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(b.runs_scored), 0) AS batsman_runs,
  COALESCE(SUM(e.extra_runs), 0) AS extra_runs,
  COALESCE(SUM(b.runs_scored), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(e.extra_runs), 0) AS total_runs
FROM
  -- deliveries with batsman-run info
  batsman_scored b
  FULL OUTER JOIN extra_runs e ON b.match_id = e.match_id AND b.over_id = e.over_id AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
  -- ensure we include overs that might appear only in one table by unioning keys
  -- create driving set of distinct match/innings/over from both tables
  -- (SQLite doesn't support FULL OUTER JOIN; emulate with UNION below)
  JOIN (
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id FROM batsman_scored
    UNION
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id FROM extra_runs
  ) d ON d.match_id = COALESCE(b.match_id, e.match_id) AND d.innings_no = COALESCE(b.innings_no, e.innings_no) AND d.over_id = COALESCE(b.over_id, e.over_id)
GROUP BY
  d.match_id,
  d.innings_no,
  d.over_id
views.description: Per match + innings + over, raw summed runs contributed by batsmen and extras separately and their combined total. Keeps rows even if one of the components is missing (treated as zero).

views.name: over_level_dominant_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  -- dominant bowler: bowler with max deliveries in that over; tie-breaker: smallest bowler id
  (SELECT bowler FROM (
     SELECT bowler, COUNT(*) AS cnt
     FROM ball_by_ball bb2
     WHERE bb2.match_id = b.match_id
       AND bb2.innings_no = b.innings_no
       AND bb2.over_id = b.over_id
       AND bb2.bowler IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY bowler
     ORDER BY cnt DESC, bowler ASC
     LIMIT 1
  )) AS bowler,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ball_by_ball bb3
     WHERE bb3.match_id = b.match_id
       AND bb3.innings_no = b.innings_no
       AND bb3.over_id = b.over_id
       AND bb3.bowler = (
         SELECT bowler FROM (
           SELECT bowler, COUNT(*) AS cnt
           FROM ball_by_ball bb4
           WHERE bb4.match_id = b.match_id
             AND bb4.innings_no = b.innings_no
             AND bb4.over_id = b.over_id
             AND bb4.bowler IS NOT NULL
           GROUP BY bowler
           ORDER BY cnt DESC, bowler ASC
           LIMIT 1
         )
       )
  ) AS bowler_ball_count,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ball_by_ball bb5
     WHERE bb5.match_id = b.match_id
       AND bb5.innings_no = b.innings_no
       AND bb5.over_id = b.over_id
  ) AS total_ball_count
FROM (
  -- distinct over-level grain from ball_by_ball
  SELECT DISTINCT match_id, innings_no, over_id
  FROM ball_by_ball
) b
views.description: Per match + innings + over, the bowler id that delivered the majority of recorded balls in that over and a count of deliveries seen for that bowler and total deliveries in the over. If multiple bowlers tie for majority, one is chosen deterministically (smallest bowler id).

views.name: match_innings_max_over
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.match_id,
  o.innings_no,
  o.over_id,
  -- dominant bowler for the over: bowler with most deliveries in that over; ties broken by smallest bowler id
  (SELECT b.bowler
   FROM ball_by_ball b
   WHERE b.match_id = o.match_id
     AND b.innings_no = o.innings_no
     AND b.over_id = o.over_id
   GROUP BY b.bowler
   ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, b.bowler ASC
   LIMIT 1) AS bowler,
  -- total runs in the over: sum of batsman runs + extra runs from batsman_scored and extra_runs tables
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs,0))
    FROM batsman_scored bs
    LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
      ON er.match_id = bs.match_id
      AND er.over_id = bs.over_id
      AND er.ball_id = bs.ball_id
      AND er.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    WHERE bs.match_id = o.match_id
      AND bs.innings_no = o.innings_no
      AND bs.over_id = o.over_id
  ), 0) AS max_over_runs
FROM
  (
    -- list all distinct match+innings+over combinations present in ball-level or over-level tables
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id
    FROM batsman_scored
    UNION
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id
    FROM extra_runs
    UNION
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id
    FROM ball_by_ball
  ) o
-- ensure one row per match_id + innings_no + over_id; downstream will pick max per match+innings
views.description: For each match and innings, the single over with the maximum combined runs (ties broken by smallest over_id) along with that over's total runs and the dominant bowler. Does not compute final average — leaves one row per match+innings for downstream aggregation.

views.name: ball_events_with_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  b.bowler,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, br.runs_scored) AS runs_scored,
  er.extra_runs,
  er.extra_type,
  b.team_batting,
  m.season_id
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_per_ball br
  ON br.match_id = b.match_id
  AND br.over_id = b.over_id
  AND br.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND br.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN match m
  ON m.match_id = b.match_id
views.description: One row per ball event combining ball_by_ball, batsman_scored, extra_runs and match to expose who batted, who bowled, runs scored on the ball, extras and the season of the match. Keeps raw per-ball measures to allow season-level aggregations later.

views.name: wicket_events_with_bowler_and_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out,
  b.bowler,
  m.season_id
FROM wicket_taken w
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
JOIN "match" m
  ON m.match_id = w.match_id
views.description: One row per wicket event joining wicket_taken to ball_by_ball and match to expose the bowler who delivered that ball and the season. Keeps the kind_out so callers can exclude specific dismissal kinds when counting wickets.

views.name: ball_by_ball_cleansed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.bowler
FROM ball_by_ball b
WHERE b.striker IS NOT NULL
  AND b.non_striker IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized ball-by-ball deliveries with non-null striker/non_striker, canonical column names and delivery identity. One row per delivery (ball) in an innings.

views.name: bowler_deliveries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler,
  b.striker,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS batsman_runs,
  COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  w.kind_out AS wicket_kind,
  w.player_out AS wicket_player_out
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken w
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
views.description: One row per legal delivery (ball_by_ball row) with the batting runs and any matched wicket and extra info denormalized for the delivery. This ties ball_by_ball to batsman_scored, wicket_taken and extra_runs so downstream aggregations can compute per-bowler balls, wickets (credited to bowler) and runs conceded off the bat excluding extras.

views.name: bowler_match_stats_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.bowler AS bowler_player_id,
  b.match_id AS match_id,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled,
  COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored), 0) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs), 0) AS extras_on_those_deliveries,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN wt.kind_out IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(wt.kind_out) <> 'run out' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS wickets_credited
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  extra_runs er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  wicket_taken wt
  ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
  AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
GROUP BY
  b.bowler,
  b.match_id
views.description: Aggregated per bowler per match raw measures: total legal balls bowled (count of deliveries), total runs conceded off the bat (sum of batsman_scored.runs_scored for deliveries by that bowler), total extras on those deliveries (sum of extra_runs.extra_runs for those deliveries), and wickets credited to the bowler (count of wicket_taken rows for those deliveries excluding run outs). Keeps one row per bowler per match to enable best-match-figures and per-bowler aggregates.

views.name: bowler_career_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bmsr.bowler_player_id AS bowler_player_id,
  SUM(bmsr.balls_bowled) AS total_balls_bowled,
  SUM(bmsr.runs_conceded_off_bat) AS total_runs_conceded_off_bat,
  SUM(bmsr.wickets_credited) AS total_wickets_credited,
  MAX(bmsr.wickets_credited) AS best_match_wickets,
  -- runs conceded in the match where the bowler took their max wickets;
  -- if multiple matches tie for max wickets, choose the minimum runs_conceded_off_bat among them
  MIN(CASE WHEN bmsr.wickets_credited = (SELECT MAX(bmsr2.wickets_credited) FROM bowler_match_stats_raw bmsr2 WHERE bmsr2.bowler_player_id = bmsr.bowler_player_id) THEN bmsr.runs_conceded_off_bat ELSE NULL END) AS best_match_runs_conceded
FROM
  bowler_match_stats_raw bmsr
GROUP BY
  bmsr.bowler_player_id
views.description: Aggregated per bowler career-level raw measures derived from per-match stats: total balls bowled, total runs conceded off the bat, total wickets credited, and best single-match bowling values (max wickets in a match and the corresponding runs conceded in that match). This view provides the raw numbers needed to compute economy, strike rate and best-match figures formatting.
